text: Plan: stage 1 broad scan of economically standard families (momentum-reversal at all horizons, trend via ma ratio, vol, skew-kurt, range position maxr-minr, beta-corr). Stage 2 refine only families with coherent sign and magnitude across neighboring lookbacks (plateau test) using vol-scaling, ts_z, and delay-decay checks to gauge OOS robustness. Stage 3 small composites of standardized components. Final picks: middle-of-plateau parameterizations from robust families, diversified across at most 2-3 mechanisms, avoiding one-off spikes to limit selection bias vs train window.

text: Findings: four independently validated mechanisms. 1) Skew term structure: short-horizon skew (5-20d) positive, 120d skew negative; the spread sub(cs_z(skew(20)), cs_z(skew(120))) earns SR 1.4 alone, robust across leg choices (10/15/20 vs 60/120) and survives 3-5d extra lag at SR 0.8+. 2) Defensive co-movement: beta and corrm negative at every window 15-250d, strongest at 120-250d, IC up to -0.012, near-zero decay under lag. 3) Vol term structure sub(cs_z(std(5)), cs_z(std(40))) positive 0.5-0.6 across variants. 4) Vol-shock reversal neg(ts_z(std(n), 250)) 0.6-1.0 across n. Composites: weight surface for spread vs single defensive term is flat at SR 1.9-2.07 around 3:1, so train differences among top variants are noise. Final picks are three mid-plateau composites that differ in skew legs and vol components to hedge parameter-selection risk rather than chase the single max. Rejected as non-robust: skew(20) standalone (horizon-fragile), maxr and short momentum (weak, sub-0.5), kurt, minr, ma families, ret momentum at all horizons.

rationale: Three mid-plateau composites of four independently validated mechanisms: short-minus-long skew term structure (positive at 5-20d, negative at 120d, robust across leg choices and extra lag), low correlation to the panel (coherent negative sign across 15-250d for both beta and corrm, minimal decay), short-over-long vol term structure, and vol-shock reversal via ts_z of std. Weight surface is flat near 3:1 spread-to-defensive (train SR 1.9-2.07 across variants), so picks differ in skew legs and vol components to hedge parameter-selection risk rather than chase the single train max.
